\chapter{Setting Out}
\label{ch:ta-setting-out}
\hlchaptermodality{48}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that it is time, that I have a journey, and that I am setting out in Tamil.}

Complete TA-C48-set-out and say all five words in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ippōdu]{\ta{இப்போது} (ippōdu) — now}

\label{lesson:TA-C48-now}



\begin{quote}
Before the new run of words: what did \emph{oruvēḷai} mean, and what did \emph{appaḍiyē} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இப்போது}}
\textbf{\ta{இப்போது}} (\emph{ippōdu}) — \textquotedblleft{}now\textquotedblright{}.

The same pattern as the word that closed the run before, wearing the near pointer instead of the far one: \emph{i-} and \emph{pōdu}, 'a time'. This time. And \emph{appōdu} is that time, then.

In speech it usually shortens to \emph{ippō}, the way English lets \textquotedblleft{}going to\textquotedblright{} collapse into \textquotedblleft{}gonna\textquotedblright{}. The full form is what you write; the short one is what you hear.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first of five words for going.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{ippōdu}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{appaḍiyē}, then \emph{ippōdu}, and hear the pointer swap ends
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இப்போது} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}now\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nēram]{\ta{நேரம்} (nēram) — time}

\label{lesson:TA-C48-time}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{ippōdu} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{நேரம்}}
\textbf{\ta{நேரம்}} (\emph{nēram}) — \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}.

Not the hour on the clock — that is \emph{maṇi}, which you already have — but time as a quantity of it: whether there is any, whether this is the right one, whether it has run out.

\emph{nēram āccu} is how a Tamil speaker says the moment has come, and it is very often the sentence that ends a visit. Nobody has to be rude about leaving if the clock can be blamed.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two: this moment, and the stuff moments are made of.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nēram}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{ippōdu}, then \emph{nēram}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{நேரம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[payaṇam]{\ta{பயணம்} (payaṇam) — a journey}

\label{lesson:TA-C48-journey}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nēram} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பயணம்}}
\textbf{\ta{பயணம்}} (\emph{payaṇam}) — \textquotedblleft{}a journey\textquotedblright{}.

Beside it Tamil also keeps \emph{pirayāṇam}, straight from Sanskrit \emph{prayāṇa}, and the pair divides the work the way \emph{nalam} and \emph{sugam} did: the shorter word is the everyday one, the longer is what goes into writing.

Somebody travelling is a \emph{payaṇi}, with the same \emph{-i} ending that made the farmer out of his field.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three, and the third one takes you somewhere.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{payaṇam}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{nēram}, then \emph{payaṇam}, and hear both endings agree
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பயணம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}a journey\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[piṟaku]{\ta{பிறகு} (piṟaku) — afterwards}

\label{lesson:TA-C48-later}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{payaṇam} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பிறகு}}
\textbf{\ta{பிறகு}} (\emph{piṟaku}) — \textquotedblleft{}afterwards\textquotedblright{}.

Underneath it is \emph{piṉ}, 'behind'. What sits behind you in space becomes what comes after you in time, and Tamil made that move so long ago that nobody hears it any more. English did the same thing with \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{}, which began as a word about the front of things.

As a way of parting it is gentle and slightly vague: \emph{piṟaku pārkkalām}, \textquotedblleft{}we'll see each other later\textquotedblright{}, promises nothing and closes the conversation kindly.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Four, and the fourth one puts off the parting.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{piṟaku}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{payaṇam}, then \emph{piṟaku}, and let the hard \emph{ṟ} land in the second
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பிறகு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}afterwards\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[puṟappaḍu]{\ta{புறப்படு} (puṟappaḍu) — to set out}

\label{lesson:TA-C48-set-out}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{piṟaku} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{புறப்படு}}
\textbf{\ta{புறப்படு}} (\emph{puṟappaḍu}) — \textquotedblleft{}to set out\textquotedblright{}.

Two pieces, both still visible. \emph{puṟam} is the outside, and \emph{paḍu} is the all-purpose ending Tamil uses when something happens to you. To \emph{puṟappaḍu} is to come to be outside — which is what leaving a house actually consists of.

\emph{nāṉ puṟappaḍugiṟēṉ} announces your departure with none of the weight of \emph{pōy varugiṟēṉ}. It is what you say at the door with your bag already in your hand.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
That closes the run: now, time, a journey, afterwards, and getting up to go.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{puṟappaḍu}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item all five in order — \emph{ippōdu}, \emph{nēram}, \emph{payaṇam}, \emph{piṟaku}, \emph{puṟappaḍu}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{புறப்படு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}to set out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
